newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CALL ENDS UP ON LATE DEMAND, GILTS EASE.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CALL ENDS UP ON LATE DEMAND, GILTS EASE.

text.p: Indian call money ended Wednesday at 8.75-9.0 percent, up from the day's opening 7.25-7.75 on late demand from banks, dealers said.
They said call money which was traded at 7.0-7.5 for most of the day, rose in late afternoon on panic borrowing from a few banks which had uncovered positions.
"Some banks were slightly desperate in the afternoon as today is the last day before reporting to the central bank," said a public sector bank dealer.
"Some stray deals took place even at 10 percent but these rates are not indicative of the market conditions."
Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on alternate Fridays. This fortnight, they report on Thursday as banks across the country are closed on Friday for independence Day.
Dealers said they expect call money to open at 5.0-6.0 percent.
Government securities were steady to slightly down in brisk trade but most of the deals were in two stocks, dealers said.
"The 11.19 percent 2005 and 12.59 percent 2004 continue to be the star attractions," said a dealer. "Most other stocks were steady....trade was quiet."
Dealers said prices fell slightly in the afternoon when some banks sold stocks after call money rose from the morning's levels.
The 12.59 percent 2004 ended at 107 rupees, off the day's high of 107.25. It ended Tuesday at 107.
The 10,85 percent 2001 slipped to 100.65 from Tuesday's 100.70-100.73.
